# gnomon

> gnomon is a terminal coding agent whose behaviour is fixed by a content-hashed `.gnomon/` directory in the repository, not by the machine. Roles are separated by the tools they are offered, every change is gated behind an approval diff by default, every step lands in one of three outcome buckets (result, refusal, apparatus_failure), and a hash-chained audit trail records what happened. It runs local models (Ollama, llama.cpp, any OpenAI-compatible server) and cloud models, per role, and `gnomon check` applies the same rules to work done by other harnesses such as Claude Code and opencode. Node 22+; MIT; pre-1.0.

Current release: v0.6.7 (2026-11-23), the latest GitHub release and what the installer gives you; also on npm as `gnomon-harness`. 5,398 tests (5,278 TypeScript, 120 Rust), green on Linux, macOS and Windows. 0.6.x is additive: a surface that declares none of its new keys behaves as under 0.5.0, and the model-free suites hold 0.5.0's figures. From 0.4.x, read the 0.5.0 upgrade notes in the CHANGELOG (Node 22+; re-run `gnomon guard install <host> --write`; reasoning replay on by default for hosted endpoints); from 0.3.x run `gnomon migrate` in each project, then re-trust it.

New in 0.6.x — security, evaluation and compliance beside governance, on the same hash-chained trail, guard and published contracts:
- Security: `gnomon security` (posture: trust, where each role's commands run, other harnesses' hooks, the audit chain); `gnomon security test` (24 model-free attack cases mapped to OWASP LLM01/02/03/06, run through the real guard as Claude Code, opencode and Cursor call it; a fresh scaffold holds 24/24, 22/22 and 15/15, and calls a host gives its hook no event for are listed as not covered, never counted as held); a repository can no longer grant itself authority (destinations need trust, provider keys only to their provider over https, a branch cannot loosen its own rules, gnomon's state refused to every tool call); the opt-in kernel sandbox `[sandbox] exec = "os"`; docs/THREAT-MODEL.md.
- Evaluation: `gnomon eval` (paired, interleaved measurement on the tasks in `.gnomon/trials/`, each judged by its own check command, of another profile, another commit's surface or, from 0.6.2, another harness's command line with `--against command:<name>`; McNemar, Wilson, thresholds declared before the run); `gnomon audit metrics` (process metrics from verified trails, and each guarded harness's sessions per host; a host's tokens are not in the guard's trail).
- Compliance: `gnomon compliance` maps gnomon evidence to 62 controls across the EU AI Act, GDPR, OWASP LLM, ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, CRA and DORA — a mapping, never a "compliant" claim, not legal advice; citations checked against the published texts, the mapping itself still wants a qualified reviewer. `gnomon compliance dataflow` lists every route, guarded harnesses included, with an opt-in `[compliance] allowed_regions` residency rule; `gnomon compliance pack` writes a hashed evidence pack, re-checked with `--verify`.

Since 0.6.2 (all opt-in or report-only; with no new key set a 0.6.7 session is byte-identical to 0.6.6): 0.6.3 shadow-test fixes (a `cd` out of the project no longer turns `gnomon guard` off; recursive readers and globs judged by what they would open; eval cells no longer hold the trial specs) and opt-in `[approval] readonly_bash = "allow"`; 0.6.4 a live trace (reasoning, prose, compact steps, delegated turns) and reasoning read in every shape the 2026 model families send it; 0.6.5 a guard fix for words that only look like globs; 0.6.6 the daily runtime (boxed terminal, nine themes, endpoint context windows read in the background), governed self-improvement (`gnomon proposals`, `gnomon memory`, `gnomon improve`; nothing reaches `.gnomon/` without acceptance), dashboard v2, Cursor hooks v2, guard adapters for Codex CLI, Qwen Code and GitHub Copilot (written from documentation, not yet verified live), `gnomon skill export`; 0.6.7 hashline edits (`edit_format = "hashline"`), a harness signature on eval reports and evidence packs, layer-tagged failure attribution (`gnomon audit attribute`; 63 of 72 hand-labelled failures before any rule was tuned, 70 after one rule fix), `gnomon eval --ablate`, a policy linter in `gnomon check`, `gnomon audit scan` (multi-step attack patterns), `gnomon security test --sandbox` (16 non-destructive containment probes), regression trials from incidents (`gnomon improve --incidents`), and trial commands running under a POSIX shell on Windows. Property suites on the release build: surface-hash fidelity 15/15 (14/14 in 0.6.2), degradations announced and recorded 17/17, injected faults disclosed 8/8, silent success 0/11, determinism 10/10. Release notes: https://github.com/eljaplacido/gnomonharness/releases/tag/v0.6.7

Recommendations (gnomon's own v0.5.0 release runs): prompt caching on Claude is on by default — about 93% of input read from cache, $0.029 instead of $0.084 per long benchmark task, no measurable change in hidden tests passed. Start from the defaults — on Claude Haiku they did at least as well as a tuned long-task recipe at about half the cost. A done check before the final answer is opt-in: it makes the final answer more honest, not the outcome better. Hybrid local-first with cloud rescue (a cloud model takes over a stuck local turn; opt-in, [roles.<name>.escalate]) is an opt-in cost mode, not a default: about 23% of cloud-only's cloud cost, -0.07 hidden-test share vs cloud-only, +0.25 vs local-only. Those figures are not for the plan-in-the-cloud hybrid that gnomon setup offers as an opt-in mode (it never suggests hybrid), which showed no advantage over cloud-only (R3R, R4H).

Shared governance: one committed `.gnomon/` policy is enforced inside Claude Code and opencode (Cursor: shell and reads) by `gnomon guard` in their pre-tool hooks, and checked for any harness at merge time by `gnomon check`; decisions land in a hash-chained trail, which `gnomon security test`, `gnomon audit metrics` and `gnomon compliance dataflow` read per host since 0.6.1. In a $0 pilot (scripted model) both hosts made identical decisions on 137/137 forced calls, no denied call ran, and 800/800 records named agent, harness and session; the detachment holes it found are fixed in 0.5.0.

Measured (pre-registered, gnomon's own results; peer figures are cited only from before November 2026): on 34 paired short Terminal-Bench tasks against opencode (2026-09-02, v0.2 line) 50.0% vs 47.1%, p = 1.0 — no difference. In November 2026, pooled over three pre-registered studies on long Terminal-Bench tasks against opencode and mini-swe-agent, no difference was shown in either direction; in the latest single study opencode turned more tasks into full solves, while gnomon cost less per task and used fewer tool calls and tokens on the same model (figures unpublished until the benchmark repository is). On 29 long Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks (gnomon 0.4.1) a tuned hosted recipe raised the hidden-test share from 0.31 to 0.58; reasoning replay alone added 16 points (H3) and is now a default. Of 167 valid hosted long-task runs, 48% hit the 30-minute cap and 68% of those never wrote the required output; ~84% of capped time is model calls, ~1% everything else including gnomon. Did not work: switching the idle nudge off locally (LG1: no gain, 1.43x tokens), the completion gate on a local model (G1-gate: no difference shown) and with a reviewer on hosted 30-minute runs (H4-lite: -10 points), and the RTX 5090 hybrid result (87% vs 84% cloud-only), which did not reproduce and is retracted. gnomon Bench Standards (draft; OVERHEAD, CHAOS, GOVERNANCE, AUDIT, HYBRID, REPORTING, LAYER) gnomon-only figures: +169 ms CPU per run over a null harness, 0.2 ms per policy decision; 17/20 faults announced; 245/280 attacks blocked with the opt-in kernel sandbox (PR #156, unreleased; 170/280 without); self-governance 27/27; audit with a git anchor 7/7, 3/3, 5/5, 0 false alarms in 48.

Install: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eljaplacido/gnomonharness/master/scripts/install.sh | sh` (Linux/macOS) or `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eljaplacido/gnomonharness/master/scripts/install.ps1 | iex` (Windows). This installs v0.6.7 with its native binaries. Then, in the project: `gnomon setup`, optionally `gnomon dashboard`, then `gnomon launch`. Or `npm i -g gnomon-harness` (no native binaries); the command is `gnomon`. To start on the new commands: `gnomon security test`, `gnomon audit metrics`, `gnomon compliance --framework eu-ai-act,gdpr`, `gnomon compliance pack --out evidence/`, `gnomon eval --against profile:<name>`.

Agents configuring gnomon for a user: follow section 11 of the guide. Never put API keys in `.gnomon/` (use `gnomon key set <endpoint>`), never guess a model id (use `gnomon endpoint list`), and verify with `echo /quit | gnomon prompt`, which makes no model call.

## Docs

- [The gnomon guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eljaplacido/gnomonharness/master/docs/GUIDE.md): what it is, architecture, install, quick start, model recipes, commands, use cases, troubleshooting, FAQ, and a step-by-step procedure for agents
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eljaplacido/gnomonharness/master/README.md): the full reference, including The Six Rules and Known Limits
- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eljaplacido/gnomonharness/master/GETTING_STARTED.md): per-platform install steps, including Windows and from source
- [Threat model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eljaplacido/gnomonharness/master/docs/THREAT-MODEL.md): each threat, the control that answers it, the evidence that it holds, and its limit
- [Governing other harnesses](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eljaplacido/gnomonharness/master/docs/GOVERNING-OTHER-HARNESSES.md): `gnomon guard` and `gnomon check` for Claude Code, opencode and Cursor
- [Security policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eljaplacido/gnomonharness/master/.github/SECURITY.md): vulnerability disclosure, supported versions, verifying what you installed, the CRA position
- [Contracts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eljaplacido/gnomonharness/master/docs/CONTRACTS.md): exit codes, enumerations, record shapes, the TOML subset gnomon parses, the `gnomon check` verdict schema
